#animals: Animals are sorted into groups by the features of their bodies. Through the doors, animals from all over the world are waiting for you!

animals:0.fact: They feed their babies with their mother's milk. They have hair on their bodies. People are mammals too!
animals:0.about:
Mammals grow their babies inside their bodies, give birth to them, and feed them milk (there are exceptions, like the platypus, which lays eggs).
They can keep their body temperature about the same all the time, so they can live in cold places and hot places. Whales, bats and humans are all mammals.

animals:1.fact: They have feathers and a beak, and they lay eggs with hard shells. Some birds can't fly.
animals:1.about:
Birds have feathers, a beak and eggs with hard shells. There are more than 10,000 kinds in the world.
Their bones are hollow and light, so they can fly. Some birds, like penguins and ostriches, can't fly.

animals:2.fact: Their bodies are covered in scales. Snakes, lizards, turtles and crocodiles are in this group.
animals:2.about:
Reptiles protect their bodies with dry, scaly skin. Snakes, lizards, turtles and crocodiles are reptiles.
They can't make their own body heat, so they warm up by sunbathing. That's why many of them hibernate in winter.

animals:3.fact: They live in water when they are young, and can live on land when they grow up. Frogs and newts are in this group.
animals:3.about:
When amphibians are young, they live in water and breathe with gills. When they grow up, they breathe with lungs and through their skin.
The change from tadpole to frog is famous. Their skin is thin, so they are sensitive to changes in their environment.

animals:4.fact: They breathe underwater with gills and swim with fins.
animals:4.about:
Fish breathe underwater with gills and swim with fins. There are more than 30,000 kinds in the world, the most of any group of animals with backbones.
The "lateral line" on the side of their body lets them feel movement in the water.

animals:5.fact: Their bodies have 3 parts: head, chest and abdomen. They have 6 legs.
animals:5.about:
Insects have bodies in 3 parts (head, chest and abdomen) and 6 legs. More than half of all the kinds of animals on Earth are insects.
They do important jobs in nature, like helping flowers make seeds and turning fallen leaves back into soil.

#ocean: Seventy percent of the Earth's surface is ocean. The biggest animal of all lives in the sea too.

ocean:0.fact: They come to lay eggs on Japan's sandy beaches too. Most loggerhead turtles in the North Pacific are born on Japan's coasts.
ocean:0.about:
With its big head and strong jaws, it can crush hard shells and crabs.
On summer nights, the female digs a hole in the sand and lays about 100 eggs. As soon as the babies hatch, they head for the sea and travel across the Pacific for many years. Sometimes they eat plastic rubbish in the sea by mistake, thinking it is a jellyfish. This is a big problem.

ocean:1.fact: The biggest animal in the history of the Earth. It can grow to nearly 30 m long, bigger than any dinosaur!
ocean:1.about:
It can weigh up to 150 tonnes. Its heart alone weighs about as much as a small car.
Even though it is so big, it eats tiny shrimp-like animals called krill. It eats several tonnes of them a day. Long ago, people hunted so many that their numbers fell, but now they are protected all over the world.

ocean:2.fact: Each dolphin has its own "name whistle," and they call each other with it.
ocean:2.about:
Dolphins are not fish. They are mammals, just like us. They breathe through a "blowhole" on top of their head.
They are good at "echolocation": they make sounds and listen to the echoes to learn what is around them. They are very clever, and they work together to catch fish.

ocean:3.fact: The biggest fish in the world. But it eats tiny plankton. It never attacks people.
ocean:3.about:
It can be more than 12 m long, about the size of a bus.
It swims with its huge mouth open and filters plankton and small fish out of the seawater. The white spots on its body are different on every shark, so scientists use them to tell sharks apart. You can see one at an aquarium in Okinawa.

ocean:4.fact: It breaks open shellfish with a stone on its tummy. When it sleeps, it wraps seaweed around its body so it doesn't drift away.
ocean:4.about:
Sea otters have the thickest fur of any animal, so their skin stays dry even in the cold sea.
It keeps a favourite stone in a pocket under its arm and uses it as a tool to crack shells on its tummy. It eats sea urchins, so it has an important job: it stops sea urchins from eating up the seaweed forests.

ocean:5.fact: A big ray that can be 7 m wide. It moves its fins like wings and swims as if it is flying through the sky.
ocean:5.about:
Mantas are relatives of sharks. They slowly move their big fins and swim as if they are flying.
They use the "head fins" at the front of their head to scoop plankton into their mouths. For their body size, they have big brains, and they are said to be among the cleverest fish.

ocean:6.fact: A rare animal that eats only sea grass. Some say it gave people the idea for mermaid stories.
ocean:6.about:
The dugong is not a whale. Scientists think it is a close relative of the elephant.
It eats only the "sea grass" that grows on the sea floor, tens of kilograms a day. Where it has eaten, a trail is left on the sea floor like a path. In Japan, only a very few have been found, in the seas of Okinawa.

#polar: Polar bears live in the Arctic and penguins live in the Antarctic, so the two never meet!

polar:0.fact: Its fur looks white, but it is actually see-through. The skin under the fur is black.
polar:0.about:
It lives on the ice of the Arctic and is the biggest meat-eating animal on land.
Thick fat and two layers of fur keep out the cold. It waits by holes in the ice and catches seals. When the Earth gets warmer and the sea ice shrinks, it can't hunt.

polar:1.fact: The father keeps the egg warm on his feet. During the cold winter, he waits for two months without eating anything.
polar:1.about:
It is the biggest penguin, more than 1 m tall.
In the Antarctic winter, it can be minus 40 °C. The fathers huddle together in a "huddle" and take turns moving between the outside and the inside to survive the cold. In 2026, because the sea ice is shrinking, it was listed as "Endangered."

polar:2.fact: It hooks its long tusks on the ice to pull its heavy body up out of the water.
polar:2.about:
Both males and females have long tusks, and they can grow to 1 m.
They use their tusks to pull themselves onto the ice and to show how strong they are to others in the group. They use the many whiskers around their mouths to find shellfish on the sea floor.

polar:3.fact: Its fur turns pure white in winter and brown in summer.
polar:3.about:
A fox that is very tough in the cold. Even minus 50 °C is fine for it.
It has small ears and fur on the soles of its feet, so it doesn't lose body heat. It hears lemmings moving under the snow, jumps and dives into the snow to catch them.

polar:4.fact: The long horn on its head is actually a tooth! It can grow to nearly 3 m.
polar:4.about:
A kind of whale called the "unicorn of the sea." The long horn is a left tooth that keeps growing.
The tusk has nerves inside, and scientists think it may sense things like the water temperature. In winter, it lives among the ice, breathing through gaps in it.

polar:5.fact: In the Arctic summer, the sun never sets all day. That's why snowy owls hunt in the daytime too.
polar:5.about:
An owl with white feathers that blends in with the snow. The males are almost pure white, and the females have black spots.
Even its toes are covered in feathers, so it is tough in the cold. Its hearing is very good, and it can hear small animals under the snow.

polar:6.fact: The only kind of deer where both males and females have antlers.
polar:6.about:
A deer that lives in big herds in the far north. It is also famous for pulling Santa Claus's sleigh.
In winter, it digs through the snow to eat lichen. Some herds travel thousands of kilometres a year. The Sámi people of northern Europe have lived with reindeer for a very long time.

#rainforest: A forest that is warm all year round and gets lots of rain. More than half of the world's living things are said to live here.

rainforest:0.fact: Every night it builds a new bed in the trees to sleep in. "Orangutan" means "person of the forest" in Malay.
rainforest:0.about:
One of the "great apes," our close relatives. In "orangutan," "orang" means person and "utan" means forest.
It spends most of its time in the trees and swings from tree to tree with its long arms. As the jungles shrink, it has fewer places to live and is in great danger.

rainforest:1.fact: A gentle animal that lives in a family. The leader male has a silver back, so he is called a "silverback."
rainforest:1.about:
Gorillas are big, but they are usually very calm, and they eat almost only plants.
They live in a family led by a male, and every night they make beds of leaves to sleep in. Beating their chests ("drumming") is a signal to avoid a fight.

rainforest:2.fact: Every tiger's stripes are different, just like people's fingerprints. It is the biggest animal in the cat family.
rainforest:2.about:
The biggest member of the cat family. It likes water and is a good swimmer.
It lives alone and hunts at night or in the evening. 100 years ago, there were said to be 100,000 tigers in the world, but now there are about 5,000. Thanks to protection in places like India, their numbers are slowly growing.

rainforest:3.fact: It has a strong beak that can crack hard nuts. It is a bird that lives a very long time.
rainforest:3.about:
A parrot with bright red, yellow and blue feathers that lives in the forests of South America.
It has a powerful beak for cracking hard nuts, and it holds its food with its toes while it eats. Pairs often stay together for life.

rainforest:4.fact: Unusually for a cat, it loves water. It is a very good swimmer.
rainforest:4.about:
The biggest cat in the Americas. It looks like a leopard, but a jaguar has small dots inside its spots.
Its bite is very strong, and it sometimes catches caimans (a kind of crocodile) in rivers.

rainforest:5.fact: It moves so slowly that tiny algae grow in its fur, and it can even look green.
rainforest:5.about:
It spends most of the day hanging from trees, and it can sleep for 15 to 20 hours.
It moves slowly to save energy, because it lives only on leaves, which don't have much nutrition. Once a week, it climbs down from the tree to go to the toilet.

rainforest:6.fact: Its legs have stripes like a zebra, but it is actually related to the giraffe. It can clean its own ears with its long tongue.
rainforest:6.about:
A shy animal that lives only deep in the forests of the Democratic Republic of the Congo in Africa.
Until a little over 100 years ago, even European scientists didn't know about it. It wraps its tongue, which is over 30 cm long, around leaves to eat them.

#savanna: Wide grasslands with only a few trees. There is a rainy season and a dry season.

savanna:0.fact: Unusually for a cat, it lives in a group called a "pride."
savanna:0.about:
It is called the "king of the beasts." Lions live in a group (a pride), and mostly the females work together to hunt.
The male's mane is a sign of strength. Its roar can be heard up to 8 km away. Besides Africa, lions also live in Gir National Park in India.

savanna:1.fact: The biggest animal on land. It flaps its big ears to cool its body.
savanna:1.about:
The biggest animal on land. Its trunk is made of more than 40,000 muscles, so it can suck up water and pick things up.
It eats more than 100 kg of plants a day. Elephants care a lot about their family, and a grandmother elephant leads the herd. People are still working to protect them from poachers who want their tusks.

savanna:2.fact: Its neck is very long, but it has the same number of neck bones as a person: 7.
savanna:2.about:
It is more than 5 m tall. Its long neck lets it eat leaves from tall trees that other animals can't reach.
It sleeps standing up, only for short times. With its 50 cm tongue, it can even eat thorny acacia leaves.

savanna:3.fact: Every zebra's stripes are different. Scientists think the stripes help keep insects away.
savanna:3.about:
The black and white stripes are different on every zebra.
One idea is that when zebras stand together, their stripes blend, so it is hard for a lion to pick out just one. Every year, they go on a great journey with wildebeest to find grass.

savanna:4.fact: The fastest animal on land. It can run at nearly 100 km per hour.
savanna:4.about:
The speed champion: it can go from standing still to nearly 100 km per hour in 3 seconds.
But it can only run at full speed for about 30 seconds. Its thin body, long legs and long tail for balance are the secrets of its speed. The black lines on its face are said to cut down the glare of the sun.

savanna:5.fact: In the daytime it stays in the water of rivers and ponds, and at night it comes out onto land to eat grass.
savanna:5.about:
The third heaviest animal on land (2 to 3 tonnes). It doesn't swim. It walks along the bottom of the river.
A reddish liquid that comes out of its skin like sweat works like sunscreen. It eats plants, but it guards its territory fiercely.

savanna:6.fact: It's called the "white rhino," but its body isn't white. People say the name came from its wide mouth.
savanna:6.about:
The biggest kind of rhino.
At one time there were only a few dozen left, but thanks to protection in places like South Africa, there are now tens of thousands. Poachers still hunt them for their horns, so protecting them is important.

#desert: Places where it hardly ever rains. It is very hot in the daytime, and it can get cold at night.

desert:0.fact: Its pale body reflects the sunlight. It gets water from the plants it eats, so it can live with almost no drinking water.
desert:0.about:
A pale antelope that lives in the Sahara Desert. It has long, twisted horns.
It rests in the hot daytime and moves around in the cool night. Today there are thought to be fewer than 100 in the wild, so it is in great danger.

desert:1.fact: Its big ears let out body heat. It can even hear prey moving under the sand.
desert:1.about:
The smallest fox in the world. It has huge ears (15 cm) for its body size.
It digs holes in the desert sand to live in and rests in its cool burrow during the day. It hardly needs to drink, because it gets water from its food.

desert:2.fact: While the others eat, one meerkat stands up and keeps watch. When it sees an enemy, it calls out to warn them.
desert:2.about:
Meerkats live together in groups of about 30 and help each other.
The lookout stands on its back legs and calls out when it sees a hawk or other danger. They are not hurt much by scorpion poison, and adults are known to teach their young how to eat scorpions.

desert:3.fact: It eats thousands of ants a day. Water travels along grooves in its spiky body all the way to its mouth.
desert:3.about:
A lizard covered in spikes. But it is only about 20 cm long, and it is a gentle animal that eats only ants.
The bump on the back of its neck is a "fake head." When an enemy attacks, it hides its real head.

desert:4.fact: It once disappeared from the wild. But people raised them and put them back into the wild, and their numbers grew.
desert:4.about:
A desert antelope with two long, straight horns. From the side, the two horns look like one, and some say this started the legend of the unicorn.
It disappeared from the wild in 1972, but animals raised in zoos were returned to the wild, and now there are more than 1,000.

desert:5.fact: A newborn baby is only about 2 cm long. It grows big in its mother's pouch.
desert:5.about:
It hops on its back legs and can go faster than 50 km per hour. It can jump as far as 8 m in one hop.
It uses its thick tail for balance. It is a symbol of Australia and is even shown on coins.

desert:6.fact: It has fur on the soles of its feet, so it can walk on hot sand.
desert:6.about:
A small cat that lives in the desert. It looks just like a pet cat.
The fur on its feet protects them from the hot sand and also makes its footprints hard to see. It hardly drinks water and gets moisture from the animals it catches.

#forest: Forests in places with spring, summer, autumn and winter. Nuts and leaves are food for the animals.

forest:0.fact: It spends almost half the day eating. It eats more than 10 kg of bamboo a day.
forest:0.about:
A kind of bear that lives in the bamboo forests of China's mountains. Some say its black and white pattern helps it hide in snow and shadows.
Its relatives eat meat, but now 99% of its food is bamboo. A wrist bone called a "false thumb" helps it hold bamboo well.

forest:1.fact: The name "panda" was actually given to the red panda first, before the giant panda.
forest:1.about:
An animal about the size of a cat that lives in mountain forests like those of the Himalayas. It is not closely related to the giant panda.
It wraps its fluffy tail around its body to keep warm. It is very popular at zoos in Japan.

forest:2.fact: Eucalyptus leaves don't have much nutrition, so koalas sleep nearly 20 hours a day to save energy.
forest:2.about:
Koalas live in the eucalyptus forests of Australia and spend almost all day in the trees.
Eucalyptus leaves are poisonous, but koalas have special guts that can digest them. One idea is that "koala" means "doesn't drink water" in an Aboriginal language.

forest:3.fact: In Japan it lives in Hokkaido. It eats a lot in autumn and hibernates in a den in winter.
forest:3.about:
The brown bears of Hokkaido are the biggest land animals in Japan.
In autumn they eat lots of salmon and nuts to get fat, and in winter they hibernate in a den. The mothers give birth in the den during hibernation. When people go into the mountains, they make noise with bells so they don't meet one.

forest:4.fact: It lives in a family pack and talks to the others by howling. It is the ancestor of dogs.
forest:4.about:
A clever animal that lives and works together in a family pack.
Howling is a way to keep in touch with the pack and to tell others whose territory it is. Japan once had Japanese wolves too, but they died out more than 100 years ago. Wolves are the ancestors of today's dogs.

forest:5.fact: It has about 5,000 spines on its back. When it's scared, it rolls up into a ball.
forest:5.about:
The spines on its back are made of the same stuff as hair (keratin).
It is active at night and eats insects and worms. In the UK it is a popular garden visitor, but because of car accidents and loss of places to live, its numbers have fallen, and in 2024 it was listed as "Near Threatened."

forest:6.fact: It chews through trees to knock them down and builds dams in rivers. Its teeth keep growing all its life.
forest:6.about:
The "builder of the forest" chews trees down and blocks rivers to make dams.
In the pond made by the dam, it builds a safe home (a lodge) with its entrance under the water. Beaver ponds become homes for other living things too. It is Canada's national animal.

#japan-animals: Japan has many animals that live nowhere else. Tsushima in Nagasaki has a special cat too!

japan-animals:0.fact: Apart from humans, it is the monkey that lives farthest north in the world. Some of them bathe in hot springs in winter.
japan-animals:0.about:
A monkey that lives only in Japan. It has a red face and a red bottom.
The monkeys at Jigokudani in Nagano that bathe in hot springs in winter are famous around the world. The monkeys on Koshima in Miyazaki are known for washing sweet potatoes in seawater before eating them.

japan-animals:1.fact: A wild cat that lives only on Tsushima in Nagasaki. There are said to be only about 100 of them.
japan-animals:1.about:
A wild cat that lives only on Tsushima, Nagasaki. It is a little bigger than a pet cat and has white spots on the backs of its ears.
There are very few of them, and it is a national natural monument. To stop them being hit by cars, there are "Watch out for wild cats" signs on Tsushima.

japan-animals:2.fact: The red patch on top of its head isn't feathers. It's bare skin. Pairs dance together.
japan-animals:2.about:
One of the biggest birds in Japan. With its wings spread, it is more than 2 m wide.
At one time there were only about a dozen left in Hokkaido, but thanks to work like feeding them in winter, there are now more than 1,000. It has long been a symbol of long life.

japan-animals:3.fact: It lives only in Japan and has been chosen as a "special natural monument." It walks easily on steep mountain paths.
japan-animals:3.about:
It looks like a deer, but it is actually related to cows.
It walks lightly over steep rocks and lives alone. It rubs scent from a gland under its eyes onto trees to mark its territory.

japan-animals:4.fact: A bird that can hardly fly. It was found to be a new species in 1981, so it is a very "new" bird.
japan-animals:4.about:
A bird that lives only in the northern part of Okinawa Island (Yanbaru). It can hardly fly, but it runs very fast.
At night it climbs trees to sleep. Its numbers fell because of mongooses brought in from outside and car accidents, but thanks to protection, they are slowly growing.

japan-animals:5.fact: Its ears and legs are short, so it still looks like rabbits from long ago. It calls with a high voice at night.
japan-animals:5.about:
A rabbit called a "living fossil" that lives only on Amami Ōshima and Tokunoshima in Kagoshima.
It has short ears, and it walks more often than it hops like a normal rabbit. In 2021, the islands where it lives became a World Natural Heritage site.

japan-animals:6.fact: One of the biggest amphibians in the world. Some are more than 1 m long. It is called a "living fossil."
japan-animals:6.about:
The big ones grow to 1.5 m, making it one of the largest amphibians in the world.
It lives on the bottom of clean rivers. It can hardly see, but it notices fish and crabs by feeling the water move. It is a special national natural monument and lives for decades.

#insects: Insects are the group of animals with the most kinds on Earth. More than a million kinds have been found.

insects:0.fact: They come to lick tree sap on summer nights. The males fight with their big horns.
insects:0.about:
A favourite of summer in Japan. The male's big horn is for fighting over places where tree sap comes out.
The larva lives in the soil eating fallen leaves and rotten wood for nearly a year, then becomes a pupa, then an adult.

insects:1.fact: A butterfly that travels more than 4,000 km, from Canada to Mexico.
insects:1.about:
In autumn, they travel from Canada and the USA to forests in Mexico. In Mexico, so many gather that whole trees turn orange with butterflies.
It is an amazing butterfly: the trip back north takes several generations.

insects:2.fact: It does a "dance," wiggling its bottom, to tell the others where the flowers are.
insects:2.about:
In its whole life, one worker bee collects only about one twelfth of a teaspoon of honey. They make honey by working together.
They also carry pollen from flower to flower, which helps fruit and vegetables grow.

insects:3.fact: It can carry things that weigh dozens of times more than its own body.
insects:3.about:
Ants leave a trail of "smell" on the ground to show the others where food is.
Tens of thousands of ants can live in one nest, and they have different jobs, like the queen and the workers.

insects:4.fact: A friend of farmers: it eats the aphids that attack vegetables.
insects:4.about:
The number of black spots on its red body depends on the kind. The seven-spot ladybird has 7.
One ladybug eats thousands of aphids in its life, so it is a big help to farmers. In English it is called a ladybug (USA) or a ladybird (UK).

insects:5.fact: An insect with a glowing bottom. It signals to others with the way it flashes.
insects:5.about:
The light comes from a chemical reaction inside its body. It makes almost no heat, so it is called "cold light."
You can see fireflies near clean rivers around June. All over Japan, people work to protect rivers where fireflies can live.

insects:6.fact: It rubs its wings together to make a "chirp chirp" sound. Its ears are on its front legs.
insects:6.about:
The males rub their wings together and sing to call females. Enjoying the sound of insects on autumn nights is part of Japanese culture.
People say you can work out the temperature from how many times a cricket chirps.

insects:7.fact: It has 8 legs, so it is not an insect. Insects have 6 legs.
insects:7.about:
A spider's body has 2 parts and 8 legs. It is not an insect. It belongs to the spider group.
Spider silk is said to be stronger than steel of the same thickness. The little spiders in your house are friends that eat pests.

#birds: Birds are animals with feathers and beaks. Scientists think they are actually the descendants of dinosaurs.

birds:0.fact: It can turn its head all the way round, as much as 270 degrees. It hunts at night.
birds:0.about:
Its flat face collects sound like a satellite dish. Its left and right ears are at different heights, so it can find prey even in total darkness.
The edges of its feathers are jagged, so it can fly without making a sound.

birds:1.fact: Its eyes are very good. It can spot prey many times farther away than a person can.
birds:1.about:
A bird with eyes so good it can see a rabbit on the ground from high in the sky.
The national bird of the USA is the bald eagle. In Japan, you can see big Steller's sea eagles and white-tailed eagles in Hokkaido in winter.

birds:2.fact: It flaps its wings more than 50 times a second and can stay still in the air.
birds:2.about:
Hummingbirds are the smallest birds in the world. The bee hummingbird weighs only about 2 g.
It is the only bird that can stay still in the air and fly backwards while drinking nectar from flowers.

birds:3.fact: Its pink colour comes from the shrimp and tiny creatures it eats.
birds:3.about:
Flamingos are grey when they hatch. They slowly turn pink from the colours in the shrimp and algae they eat.
People say they stand on one leg to keep their body heat in.

birds:4.fact: The male's beautiful feathers are for showing off to the females.
birds:4.about:
Only the males spread their feathers. It is said that the more "eye spots" a male has, the more the females like him.
It is the national bird of India. The female is called a peahen, and her colours are plain.

birds:5.fact: A clever bird that can copy people's words and sounds.
birds:5.about:
Parrots and parakeets are some of the few birds that can copy human voices. Some learn hundreds of words.
They have 2 toes at the front and 2 at the back, so they can hold food skilfully.

birds:6.fact: It has an amazing power to find its way home, even from far away.
birds:6.about:
Scientists think pigeons know which way to go by sensing the position of the sun and the Earth's magnetism.
Long ago, "homing pigeons" did important work carrying letters.

birds:7.fact: The biggest bird in the world. It can't fly, but it can run at 70 km per hour. Its eggs are the biggest in the world too!
birds:7.about:
The world's biggest bird: it weighs more than 100 kg and is more than 2 m tall.
Its egg is as big as 20 to 25 chicken eggs. It can't fly, but it runs fast on its long legs.

#dinosaurs: Dinosaurs lived on Earth tens of millions of years ago. Today, we learn many things about them from fossils.

dinosaurs:0.fact: A big meat-eating dinosaur that lived in North America about 66 million years ago. Its teeth were as big as bananas!
dinosaurs:0.about:
Its name means "tyrant lizard king." Scientists think it was 12 m long and weighed about 8 tonnes.
Its bite was one of the strongest of any animal. It may also have had feathers on its body.

dinosaurs:1.fact: A plant-eating dinosaur with 3 horns on its face and a big frill.
dinosaurs:1.about:
Its name means "three-horned face." Scientists think its big frill was for protecting itself and for showing off to others.
It is said to have lived in herds.

dinosaurs:2.fact: It is known for the plates along its back and the spikes on its tail.
dinosaurs:2.about:
Scientists think the plates on its back helped control its body temperature or made it look bigger to enemies.
Its body was big, but its brain is said to have been only about the size of a walnut.

dinosaurs:3.fact: It had a very long neck and ate leaves from tall trees.
dinosaurs:3.about:
Its front legs were longer than its back legs, and it held its neck up high like a giraffe.
It weighed 30 to 50 tonnes. Scientists think it ate hundreds of kilograms of plants a day.

dinosaurs:4.fact: The biggest full skeleton fossil in Japan, found in Mukawa, Hokkaido.
dinosaurs:4.about:
An 8 m long plant-eating dinosaur found in Mukawa, Hokkaido. It is the most complete dinosaur skeleton ever found in Japan.
Its name comes from the Ainu word "kamuy" (god).

dinosaurs:5.fact: A meat-eating dinosaur found in Fukui. Fukui is a treasure house of dinosaur fossils.
dinosaurs:5.about:
A meat-eating dinosaur found in Katsuyama, Fukui. The Fukui Prefectural Dinosaur Museum is said to be one of the three greatest dinosaur museums in the world.
More dinosaur fossils have been found in Fukui than anywhere else in Japan.

dinosaurs:6.fact: A high school student found it in Fukushima in 1968. It is actually not a dinosaur but a sea reptile.
dinosaurs:6.about:
In 1968, a high school student, Suzuki Tadashi, found the fossil in Iwaki, Fukushima.
It is a "plesiosaur" about 7 m long. "Futaba" in its name is the rock layer it was found in, and "Suzuki" is the name of the person who found it.

dinosaurs:7.fact: A flying reptile. People often get this wrong, but it is not a dinosaur.
dinosaurs:7.about:
Its wings were about 7 m across. It was a flying reptile called a "pterosaur," a different group from the dinosaurs.
Scientists think it flew over the sea and caught fish to eat.

dinosaurs:8.fact: Birds are the descendants of dinosaurs that survived. Even chickens are related to dinosaurs!
dinosaurs:8.about:
66 million years ago, a huge meteorite hit the Earth, and most dinosaurs died out.
But some small feathered dinosaurs survived and became today's birds. Sparrows and pigeons are descendants of dinosaurs too.

#pets: Animals that live with us. "I have a dog." from New Horizon is here too.

pets:0.fact: Its sense of smell is thousands of times better than a person's. It learns many things from smells.
pets:0.about:
People and dogs are said to have lived together for more than 15,000 years.
Many dogs do jobs that help people, like guide dogs, police dogs and rescue dogs.

pets:1.fact: It sleeps 12 to 16 hours a day. It uses its whiskers to check whether it can fit through narrow spaces.
pets:1.about:
Cats are said to have started living with people about 10,000 years ago in the Middle East, because they protected grain from mice.
Cats purr when they are happy or feel safe.

pets:2.fact: Its long ears don't just hear sounds. They also let out body heat.
pets:2.about:
It can move its left and right ears separately and can hear sounds far away.
Its teeth keep growing all its life, so it wears them down by eating tough grass. When it is happy, it sometimes jumps up in the air.

pets:3.fact: It stuffs food into its cheek pouches and carries it back to its nest.
pets:3.about:
Hamsters are active at night, so they run on their wheels in the evening. One can run several kilometres in one night.
Its cheek pouches can hold a surprising amount of food for its body size.

pets:4.fact: A fish that first came from China. It arrived in Japan about 500 years ago.
pets:4.about:
Goldfish come from a kind of carp. They have been raised in China for more than 1,000 years, and many different shapes have been bred.
"Goldfish scooping" at summer festivals is a classic part of summer in Japan.

pets:5.fact: A small parakeet from Australia. Some can learn words.
pets:5.about:
A small parakeet that lives in big flocks in the grasslands of Australia.
In English it is also called a budgie. They come in many colours, like green, yellow and blue.

pets:6.fact: Turtles live a very long time. You may be able to live together for decades.
pets:6.about:
In English, people sometimes call turtles that live in water "turtles" and ones that live on land "tortoises."
A turtle's shell is made from its ribs and backbone, so it is part of its body.

#farm: Milk, eggs, wool… farm animals support our everyday lives.

farm:0.fact: One dairy cow gives about 25 litres of milk a day.
farm:0.about:
Holstein dairy cows are black and white. Cows have 4 stomachs and chew their grass again and again to digest it.
In Japan, Hokkaido produces the most milk.

farm:1.fact: It is actually a very clever animal that likes to be clean.
farm:1.about:
Pigs can't sweat, so they roll in mud to cool down.
Their sense of smell is very good. In France, pigs have helped people find expensive mushrooms called "truffles" in the ground.

farm:2.fact: People shear its wool to make yarn and sweaters.
farm:2.about:
One sheep gives enough wool for several sweaters a year. After it is sheared, the wool grows back.
There are said to be more than 1 billion sheep in the world.

farm:3.fact: Some chickens lay nearly 300 eggs a year.
farm:3.about:
The ancestor of the chicken is a bird from Southeast Asia called the red junglefowl.
The colour of the eggshell (white or brown) depends on the kind of chicken, and the nutrition is almost the same.

farm:4.about:
Its eyes are on the sides of its face, so it can see almost 360 degrees, everywhere except right behind it.
Tsushima in Nagasaki has a Japanese native horse called the "Taishū horse."

farm:5.fact: It can climb steep rocky mountains with ease.
farm:5.about:
The black part of a goat's eye (the pupil) is a wide rectangle, so it can see a wide area.
Cheese is also made from goat's milk. Goats eat grass, so they are sometimes used to keep grass short.

farm:6.fact: Ducklings think the first moving thing they see after hatching is their parent, and they follow it.
farm:6.about:
Ducks are mallards, wild birds that people tamed long ago.
They swim well with waterproof feathers and webbed feet. There is even a way of farming called "aigamo farming," where ducks eat the weeds and insects in rice fields.

#deepsea: The bottom of the sea, where no light reaches. People say there are living things down there that no one has ever seen.

deepsea:0.fact: Its eyes are as big as basketballs, some of the biggest eyes of any animal.
deepsea:0.about:
A huge squid that can be more than 10 m long. In 2004, Japanese scientists were the first in the world to take photos of a live one.
Its big eyes catch the faint light of the dark deep sea.

deepsea:1.fact: It lights up the "lantern" on its head to lure prey.
deepsea:1.about:
In the deep sea, where no light reaches, it lights up the "lantern" on its head to lure small fish. The light comes from bacteria living inside the lantern.
With its big mouth, it can swallow prey as big as itself.

deepsea:2.fact: More than 95% of its body is water. It has no brain and no heart.
deepsea:2.about:
Jellyfish have been on Earth for more than 500 million years. They have no brain, no heart and no bones.
There is even an amazing jellyfish that can turn young again and again. Be careful not to get stung in the sea.

deepsea:3.fact: The world's biggest crab lives in the seas of Japan. With its legs spread out, it can be more than 3 m wide.
deepsea:3.about:
It lives only in Japan, in deep seas such as Suruga Bay in Shizuoka.
Some say it can live for 100 years. Its legs are thin but very long, so with its legs spread it is about as wide as a car.

deepsea:4.fact: At one aquarium, one went more than 5 years without eating anything.
deepsea:4.about:
A relative of the pill bug that can be more than 40 cm long. It is the "cleaner of the sea," eating dead fish that sink to the deep sea floor.
It uses very little energy, so it can go without food for a long time.

deepsea:5.fact: The deepest sea in the world, about 10,900 m deep. Mount Everest would fit inside with room to spare.
deepsea:5.about:
The deepest place in the world, the "Challenger Deep," is near the island of Guam in the Pacific Ocean.
The weight of the water there is like an elephant standing on your fingertip. Even so, living things live there.

#animal-records: Fastest, biggest, longest-living… here are the animal world's record holders.

animal-records:0.fact: Nearly 30 m long. The biggest animal in the history of the Earth.
animal-records:0.about: Its body is nearly 30 m long, and it can weigh more than 150 tonnes. Its calls are said to travel hundreds of kilometres.

animal-records:1.fact: Nearly 100 km per hour. But it can't run for long.
animal-records:1.about: It reaches nearly 100 km per hour just 3 seconds after starting. But it can only run at full speed for a few hundred metres.

animal-records:2.fact: When it dives at its prey, it goes faster than 300 km per hour.
animal-records:2.about: When diving at its prey, one was recorded at 390 km per hour. That's faster than the Shinkansen.

animal-records:3.fact: More than 5 m tall. It can reach a second-floor window.
animal-records:3.about: It is already about 1.8 m tall when it is born. A baby giraffe stands up within an hour of being born.

animal-records:4.fact: It weighs more than 6 tonnes, as much as 4 or 5 cars.
animal-records:4.about: It weighs more than 6 tonnes. It flaps its ears to let out body heat.

animal-records:5.fact: A shark that some say can live about 400 years.
animal-records:5.about: It lives in the cold Arctic sea and grows only about 1 cm a year. Because it grows so slowly, scientists think it lives a very long time.

animal-records:6.fact: It weighs about 2 g, the same as two 1-yen coins.
animal-records:6.about: A bat that lives in caves in Thailand and Myanmar. Its body is about the size of a bumblebee.

#plants: Plants can't move, but they have lots of amazing tricks for surviving.

plants:0.fact: When it is a bud, it turns to follow the sun.
plants:0.about:
The seeds in the middle of the flower are lined up in beautiful spirals. This pattern is connected to "Fibonacci numbers" in maths.
Oil is made from the seeds too. It is also the national flower of Ukraine.

plants:1.fact: All Somei Yoshino cherry trees come from one single tree.
plants:1.about:
The symbol of spring in Japan. Every year, the Japan Meteorological Agency announces when the cherry trees bloom.
The cherry trees in Washington, D.C. were a gift from Tokyo in 1912.

plants:2.fact: Its spines are leaves that have changed shape. They help it keep in water.
plants:2.about:
A cactus stores water in its thick stem so it can survive dry weather.
The saguaro cactus in the deserts of the USA can grow 15 m tall.

plants:3.fact: A very fast-growing plant that can grow nearly 1 m in one day.
plants:3.about:
Bamboo is actually a kind of grass. The roots are joined underground, so a whole bamboo forest can be one single plant.
A bamboo shoot becomes a full-grown bamboo in just a few months.

plants:4.fact: A plant that snaps its leaves shut to catch insects.
plants:4.about:
There are tiny "trigger hairs" inside the leaves. When an insect touches them twice, the leaf shuts in about half a second.
It grows in soil with little nutrition, so it gets nutrition from insects.

plants:5.fact: It stores water in its thick trunk to get through the dry season.
plants:5.about:
A tree that grows in Africa and Madagascar. Some trunks are more than 10 m around.
Without its leaves, it looks like a tree planted upside down with its roots in the air, so it is called the "upside-down tree."

plants:6.fact: The biggest flower in the world. It can be about 1 m across.
plants:6.about:
A flower that blooms in the forests of Southeast Asia. It has no leaves, no stem and no roots, and it lives attached to other plants.
Its strong smell attracts flies, and they carry its pollen.

plants:7.fact: The tallest trees in the world. Some are more than 115 m tall.
plants:7.about:
A tree that grows near the sea in California, USA. It takes in water from fog and grows very tall.
The tallest one is called "Hyperion," and it is about 116 m tall.

plants:8.fact: Big cedar trees on Yakushima in Kagoshima. Some have lived for thousands of years.
plants:8.about:
Cedars that have lived more than 1,000 years in the mountains of Yakushima are called Yakusugi. The most famous one, "Jōmon Sugi," is said to be more than 2,000 years old.
In 1993, Yakushima became Japan's first World Natural Heritage site.

#weather: How's the weather? Sunny, rainy, snowy… let's look at the secrets of the weather.

weather:0.fact: Sunlight warms the ground and gives the energy that makes the weather move.
weather:0.about:
Sunlight takes about 8 minutes and 20 seconds to reach the Earth. On sunny summer days, watch out for heatstroke and drink water.
In a weather forecast, "sunny" means clouds cover 20 to 80% of the sky. If it's 0 to 10%, it's "clear."

weather:1.fact: Clouds are groups of tiny drops of water or bits of ice floating in the sky.
weather:1.about:
When clouds cover more than 90% of the sky, it is "cloudy."
Sometimes the shape of the clouds tells you about the weather. People say that when you see "sheep clouds," the weather often turns bad.

weather:2.fact: When the drops in a cloud join together and get heavy, they fall as rain.
weather:2.about:
Raindrops are not shaped like tears. They are flat on the bottom, like a little bun.
The long rainy season in Japan around June is called "tsuyu." It is important rain for growing rice.

weather:3.fact: Almost all snowflakes have a beautiful six-sided shape.
weather:3.about:
The shape of a snowflake changes with the temperature and humidity in the cloud. The scientist Nakaya Ukichirō said, "Snow is a letter sent from the sky."
Hokkaido, Tōhoku and Hokuriku are areas with lots of snow.

weather:4.fact: Light is much faster than sound, so you see the flash before you hear the rumble.
weather:4.about:
Lightning is electricity made when bits of ice in a cloud bump into each other. Count the seconds between the flash and the sound and multiply by 340 m to find out how far away the lightning is.
When you hear thunder, go inside a building.

weather:5.fact: In Japan, people say a rainbow has 7 colours, but different countries count the colours differently.
weather:5.about:
Stand with the sun behind you and look at the sky after rain to find one. Light bends inside the raindrops and splits into colours.
In English, the 7 colours are red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet.

weather:6.fact: In the middle, the "eye of the typhoon," the wind can be weak and the sky clear.
weather:6.about:
A huge spinning storm that starts over warm seas in the south. Typhoons come near Japan from summer to autumn.
The same kind of storm is called a hurricane near America and a cyclone in the Indian Ocean.

weather:7.fact: Wind is moving air. It happens because of differences between warm air and cold air.
weather:7.about:
Wind happens when air flows from places with high air pressure to places with low air pressure.
"Haru-ichiban" is the first strong south wind at the start of spring.

#solar-system: Eight planets go around the Sun. The Earth is one of them.

solar-system:0.fact: It is about as wide as 109 Earths in a row. It is the star that shines in the middle of the solar system.
solar-system:0.about:
The Sun is a star about 150 million km from the Earth. Its centre is about 15 million °C.
Without the Sun's light and heat, nothing on Earth could live.

solar-system:1.fact: The planet closest to the Sun. Its year is only 88 days long.
solar-system:1.about:
The closest planet to the Sun, and the smallest. It has almost no air, so it gets to 400 °C in the day and minus 170 °C at night.
The name Mercury comes from a fast-running god in Roman myths.

solar-system:2.fact: The hottest planet, covered in thick clouds and over 450 °C.
solar-system:2.about:
It shines brightly at dawn and in the evening, so it is called the "morning star" and the "evening star."
It is about the same size as the Earth, but its thick clouds make it very hot. It also spins the opposite way to the Earth.

solar-system:3.fact: Our planet, which has water and air.
solar-system:3.about:
The Earth is at "just the right" distance from the Sun for water to stay liquid. About 70% of its surface is sea.
The Earth spins once a day and goes around the Sun once a year.

solar-system:4.fact: The red planet. It has a mountain more than twice as tall as Mount Everest.
solar-system:4.about:
It looks red because its ground has lots of rusty iron in it.
There are signs that water once flowed there, and rovers are still looking for signs of life. There are plans to send people there too.

solar-system:5.fact: The biggest planet. About 1,300 Earths would fit inside it.
solar-system:5.about:
A giant planet made of gas. The "Great Red Spot" on its surface is a storm so big the Earth could fit inside it.
More than 90 moons have been found around it.

solar-system:6.fact: Its rings are bits of ice and rock. It is so light it would float on water.
solar-system:6.about:
Its beautiful rings are made of lots and lots of bits of ice and rock. The rings are very wide, but in thin places they are only tens of metres thick.
Its moon Titan has a thick atmosphere and lakes of methane.

solar-system:7.fact: A strange planet that spins while lying on its side.
solar-system:7.about: An icy planet that looks blue-green. It is tipped over on its side as it spins, so at its north pole there are 42 years of daytime followed by 42 years of night.

solar-system:8.fact: The strongest winds in the solar system blow here.
solar-system:8.about:
The planet farthest from the Sun. It takes about 165 years to go around the Sun once.
Its winds can reach 2,000 km per hour.

#moon-stars: Let's look up at the night sky. Every star has a story.

moon-stars:0.fact: The Moon always shows the same side to the Earth. We can't see its far side from Earth.
moon-stars:0.about:
The Moon goes around the Earth about once every 27 days. It seems to change shape because the part lit by the Sun changes.
In Japan, people see "a rabbit making mochi" in the Moon's patterns, but in other countries people see things like "a crab" or "a woman's face."

moon-stars:1.fact: There are 88 constellations in the sky. Your birthday star sign is one of them.
moon-stars:1.about:
Long ago, people joined stars with lines and imagined animals and people from myths. These are constellations.
You see different constellations in the Northern and Southern Hemispheres. In the Southern Hemisphere you can see the "Southern Cross."

moon-stars:2.fact: A star that hardly moves. For a very long time it has shown people which way is north.
moon-stars:2.about:
The North Star is almost straight above the Earth's axis, so it seems to hardly move.
To find it, follow the edge of the Big Dipper's cup and go 5 times as far. It guided travellers and sailors long ago.

moon-stars:3.fact: Orihime and Hikoboshi from the Tanabata story are stars that shine on either side of the Milky Way.
moon-stars:3.about:
The Milky Way is our galaxy, the one our solar system is in, seen from the inside. Hundreds of billions of stars are gathered there.
In Japanese it is called "the river of heaven."

moon-stars:4.fact: A tiny bit of dust from space that glows when it hits the air.
moon-stars:4.about:
Most shooting stars are tiny bits of dust about the size of a grain of sand.
You can see lots of shooting stars in the Perseid meteor shower every August and the Geminid meteor shower in December.

moon-stars:5.fact: When the Moon passes in front of the Sun, the Sun looks hidden.
moon-stars:5.about:
The Sun is about 400 times bigger than the Moon, but it is also about 400 times farther from the Earth, so they look exactly the same size. That's why the Moon can cover the Sun perfectly.
When you watch a solar eclipse, always use special eclipse glasses.

moon-stars:6.fact: An object in space with gravity so strong that not even light can escape.
moon-stars:6.about:
One can form when a very heavy star comes to the end of its life.
In 2019, a team of scientists from around the world took the first ever photo of a black hole's shadow. Japanese scientists were part of the team.

#space-explore: People have ridden rockets to reach space. Japan has done lots of great work too.

space-explore:0.fact: In 1969, people stood on the Moon for the first time.
space-explore:0.about:
In July 1969, the American astronaut Neil Armstrong stood on the Moon and said, "That's one small step for man, one giant leap for mankind."
So far, 12 people have stood on the Moon.

space-explore:1.fact: Astronauts live on it as it goes around the Earth about once every 90 minutes.
space-explore:1.about:
A space laboratory built together by the USA, Russia, Japan, Europe, Canada and others. It flies about 400 km up.
It has a Japanese laboratory called "Kibō." Sometimes you can see it as a bright dot gliding across the night sky.

space-explore:2.fact: A Japanese space probe. In 2010 it brought sand from the asteroid "Itokawa" back to Earth.
space-explore:2.about: It was launched in 2003 and travelled 6 billion km over 7 years. It got through many problems, like engine trouble, and made it home, so its return was called a "miracle."

space-explore:3.fact: It brought rocks from the asteroid "Ryugu" back and delivered them to Earth in 2020.
space-explore:3.about:
It made an artificial crater on the asteroid Ryugu and brought back rocks from under the surface.
Amino acids, building blocks of life, were found in the Ryugu rocks.

space-explore:4.fact: In 2014, Wakata Kōichi became the first Japanese commander of the space station.
space-explore:4.about:
The first Japanese person to go to space was Akiyama Toyohiro in 1990. Many Japanese people, like Mōri Mamoru and Mukai Chiaki, have done great work in space.
In space your body floats, so your bed is a sleeping bag fixed to the wall.

space-explore:5.fact: Japanese ramen and curry have been made so that astronauts can eat them in space.
space-explore:5.about:
In space, food floats around, so space food is made so it doesn't crumble and spill.
Japanese space food includes curry, ramen and yōkan (sweet bean jelly).

space-explore:6.fact: Japan's rockets are launched from Tanegashima in Kagoshima.
space-explore:6.about:
Japan's biggest rocket launch site, on Tanegashima in Kagoshima. It is said to be "the most beautiful rocket base in the world."
Tanegashima is also known as the island where guns first came to Japan, in 1543.

#regions: I want to go to ___. There are more than 190 countries in the world. Where would you like to go?

regions:0.fact: More than half of the world's people live here. Japan is an Asian country too.
regions:0.about:
The biggest region in the world, with 48 countries. It has every kind of nature, from the Himalayas with Mount Everest to deserts, rainforests and snowy lands.
Many countries here eat rice and use chopsticks.

regions:1.fact: Lots of small countries are close together, so you can travel from country to country by train.
regions:1.about:
A region with more than 40 countries. It is easy to travel between them by train or car.
Many countries use the same money, the "euro." There are lots of old castles, churches and art museums.

regions:2.fact: The region with the most countries: more than 50.
regions:2.about:
There are more than 50 countries, and more than 2,000 languages are said to be spoken.
The Sahara Desert, savannas, rainforests, huge waterfalls… Scientists think it is also where humans first appeared.

regions:3.fact: The region with the USA, Canada, Mexico and other countries.
regions:3.about:
The region with the USA, Canada, Mexico and the countries of Central America and the Caribbean.
The north is a world of ice, and the south has warm seas. English, Spanish, French and other languages are spoken.

regions:4.fact: A region with the Amazon River and a huge rainforest.
regions:4.about:
There are 12 countries. It has the world's biggest rainforest, the Amazon, and the long Andes mountains.
Most countries speak Spanish, and Brazil speaks Portuguese.

regions:5.fact: Australia and lots of island countries in the Pacific Ocean.
regions:5.about:
The continent of Australia and thousands of islands in the Pacific. Many animals, like kangaroos and koalas, live only here.
It is in the Southern Hemisphere, so the seasons are the opposite of Japan's. Christmas is in summer!

regions:6.fact: A continent with no countries. Scientists live there to do research.
regions:6.about:
An icy continent at the very south of the Earth. It has no countries, and scientists from many countries do research there.
Japan has "Shōwa Station" there. It is the coldest place on Earth, and once it was minus 89 °C.

#asia: Let's start with countries near Japan. Can you say "hello" in their languages?

asia:0.fact: The Great Wall of China is more than 20,000 km long. That's half way around the Earth.
asia:0.about:
The country with the second most people in the world. It has a long history and gave the world paper, the compass and printing.
Kanji (Chinese characters) were also born in China and came to Japan. It is the home of the giant panda too.

asia:1.fact: The Hangul alphabet was made nearly 600 years ago.
asia:1.about:
One of the closest countries to Japan. On a clear day, you can see Busan in South Korea from Tsushima in Nagasaki.
K-pop, Korean dramas, kimchi, bibimbap… lots of Korean culture is popular in Japan too. People eat with chopsticks and a spoon.

asia:2.fact: The country with the most people in the world. More than 1.4 billion people live there.
asia:2.about:
In 2023 it became the country with the most people in the world. It is said that the number "0" was first thought up in India.
Curry tastes different in each area, and many people eat with their hands. There are many languages, and 17 of them are written on the banknotes.

asia:3.fact: The elephant is the symbol of Thailand. In April there is a festival where people splash water on each other.
asia:3.about:
A country in Southeast Asia called the "Land of Smiles." In Thai, the country's name means "land of the free."
Its food mixes sweet, sour, spicy and salty flavours. At the April New Year festival, "Songkran," people celebrate by splashing water on each other.

asia:4.fact: A long country shaped like the letter S.
asia:4.about:
A country that is long from north to south. The north is cold in winter, and the south is hot all year.
There are lots of rice dishes, like "phở" noodles made from rice flour and fresh spring rolls. People use chopsticks like in Japan, and there are lots and lots of motorbikes.

asia:5.fact: A country made of more than 7,000 islands.
asia:5.about:
A country made of more than 7,000 islands. English is an official language too, so lots of people speak English.
It grows lots of bananas and mangoes, and many of the bananas in Japanese supermarkets come from the Philippines.

asia:6.fact: With more than 17,000 islands, it is one of the countries with the most islands in the world.
asia:6.about:
The world's biggest island country, with more than 17,000 islands. It has the fourth most people in the world.
The world's biggest lizard, the Komodo dragon, and orangutans live here. In "nasi goreng," "nasi" means rice and "goreng" means fried.

asia:7.fact: A country with more horses than people. People live in tents called "gers" that they can put up and take down.
asia:7.about:
A country with no sea and wide grasslands. About 3.5 million people live there, and there are more horses than people.
At the summer festival "Naadam," there are wrestling, horse racing and archery contests. In Japanese sumo, wrestlers from Mongolia do very well too.

#europe: Europe has lots of small countries. When the country changes, the language and food change too.

europe:0.fact: A country made of four parts: England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.
europe:0.about:
Its full name is "the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland." It is the country where English was born.
Many sports, like football, tennis and rugby, started here. Red double-decker buses and Big Ben are famous.

europe:1.fact: The Eiffel Tower in Paris is 330 m tall. It was built in 1889.
europe:1.about:
One of the countries with the most tourists in the world. Paris has the Eiffel Tower and the Louvre Museum.
There are very many kinds of bread and cheese. People say there are more than 1,000 kinds of cheese.

europe:2.fact: The country is shaped like a long boot.
europe:2.about:
In the capital, Rome, buildings from more than 2,000 years ago are still standing.
It is the home of pizza and pasta, and there are hundreds of pasta shapes. Leonardo da Vinci, who painted the Mona Lisa, was Italian too.

europe:3.fact: A country with very many kinds of bread and sausages.
europe:3.about:
The country with the most people in the EU. It is good at making cars and machines.
Many famous composers, like Beethoven and Bach, were born here. It is also the home of Christmas markets and Grimms' fairy tales.

europe:4.fact: It is famous for "La Tomatina," a festival where people throw tomatoes at each other.
europe:4.about:
A bright country with lots of sunny days all year round. Dinner is usually very late, around 9 o'clock at night.
It is famous for the Sagrada Família, flamenco and football. More than 500 million people in the world speak Spanish.

europe:5.fact: The land of saunas. It has a Santa Claus Village.
europe:5.about:
The "land of forests and lakes." More than 70% of the country is forest, and there are more than 180,000 lakes.
In winter the days are very short, and you can sometimes see the northern lights in the night sky. It is also famous for its excellent schools.

europe:6.fact: The country where the Olympics were born, about 2,800 years ago.
europe:6.about:
More than 2,000 years ago, ancient Greece gave the world the Olympics, theatre and democracy.
The Aegean Sea has islands with white houses and blue roofs. Its food uses lots of olive oil.

europe:7.fact: In the Edo period, it traded with Japan on Dejima in Nagasaki.
europe:7.about:
A quarter of the country is below sea level. People built the country by pumping out water with windmills.
It is the land of tulips, and people say there are more bicycles than people. In the Edo period, it brought medicine and science to Japan through Dejima in Nagasaki.

#africa: Africa is said to have more than 50 countries and more than 2,000 languages.

africa:0.fact: The pyramids were built about 4,500 years ago.
africa:0.about:
An ancient civilisation grew up along the Nile, one of the longest rivers in the world.
It is famous for the pyramids, the Sphinx and hieroglyphs (ancient writing). Most of the country is desert, so people live near the river.

africa:1.fact: A country where many strong marathon runners come from.
africa:1.about:
A country right on the equator. Safaris to see lions, elephants and giraffes on the savanna are popular.
"Jambo" is a greeting in Swahili. Growing up in towns high in the mountains is said to be one secret of their marathon strength.

africa:2.fact: It has Kilimanjaro (5,895 m), the highest mountain in Africa.
africa:2.about:
It has Mount Kilimanjaro, the highest mountain in Africa, and Serengeti National Park, famous for its great animal migration.
Swahili is widely spoken. "Hakuna matata" means "no worries" in Swahili.

africa:3.fact: An unusual country with 3 capital cities. There are even penguins on its beaches.
africa:3.about:
The southernmost country in Africa. It has 3 capitals: Pretoria, Cape Town and Bloemfontein.
It has 12 official languages and is called the "Rainbow Nation." On the beaches near Cape Town, you can see wild penguins.

africa:4.fact: It has a town called "Chefchaouen," where the whole town is painted blue.
africa:4.about:
It is in the north-west of Africa, only about 14 km across the sea from Spain in Europe.
It is famous for busy markets (souks) and the blue town of Chefchaouen. People cook in a pot called a "tagine," which has a lid shaped like a pointed hat.

africa:5.fact: The world's second biggest grower of cacao, which chocolate is made from.
africa:5.about:
A country in West Africa. It grows cacao, the main ingredient of chocolate, and much of the cacao in Japanese chocolate comes from Ghana.
It is famous for a brightly coloured cloth called "kente." It is also where Noguchi Hideyo did his research on yellow fever.

africa:6.fact: Many living things, like lemurs, live only here.
africa:6.about:
The fourth biggest island in the world. It split away from the mainland a very long time ago, so lots of living things are found only here.
It is famous for lemurs and its avenue of huge baobab trees.

#americas: The countries of North and South America. English, Spanish, Portuguese and other languages are spoken.

americas:0.about:
A big country made of 50 states. It has the third most people in the world.
People from all over the world live there, and lots of its culture, like hamburgers, jazz, baseball and movies, has spread around the world. It is also where Ohtani Shohei plays baseball.

americas:1.fact: The second biggest country in the world. Its flag has a maple leaf on it.
americas:1.about:
The second biggest country in the world, after Russia. But only about 40 million people live there, so there is lots of wild nature.
It has 2 official languages, English and French. The red leaf on its flag is a sugar maple, and maple syrup is made from its sap.

americas:2.fact: Corn and chocolate spread to the rest of the world from this area.
americas:2.about:
A country where the ancient Maya and Aztec civilisations grew. It has pyramids too.
Corn, tomatoes, chilli peppers and chocolate (cacao) spread around the world from this area. Its colourful festivals and music are famous too.

americas:3.fact: The country with the most descendants of people who moved there from Japan.
americas:3.about:
The biggest country in South America. Much of the Amazon rainforest is in Brazil.
Its football team is very strong and has won the World Cup 5 times. Japanese people started moving there more than 100 years ago, and many Japanese-Brazilians still live there.

americas:4.fact: It has "Machu Picchu," ruins on top of a mountain. It is the home of the potato.
americas:4.about:
A country in the Andes mountains. It has Machu Picchu, ruins from the Inca Empire.
It is the home of the potato, and Peru has thousands of kinds of potatoes. Alpacas and llamas are Peruvian animals too.

americas:5.fact: The country where the dance music "tango" was born.
americas:5.about:
A very long country from north to south. Its southern tip is close to Antarctica, and there are penguins there too.
People raise cattle on wide grasslands called the "pampas" and love barbecue ("asado"). It is the land of football and tango.

#oceania: Big Australia and lots of island countries in the Pacific Ocean.

oceania:0.fact: People say there are more kangaroos than people.
oceania:0.about:
An unusual country that covers a whole continent by itself. Kangaroos, koalas, platypuses and many other animals live only here.
It is in the Southern Hemisphere, so its seasons are the opposite of Japan's. December is summer, and some people spend Christmas at the beach.

oceania:1.fact: A country with far more sheep than people.
oceania:1.about:
A country of 2 big islands and many small ones. It has mountains, glaciers, hot springs and volcanoes.
It values the culture of the Māori, its first people. "Kia ora" is a greeting in Māori. The kiwi, a bird that can't fly, is the country's symbol.

oceania:2.fact: An island country in the south with more than 300 islands.
oceania:2.about:
An island country in the South Pacific, with warm seas and coral reefs.
"Bula!" is a cheerful greeting. Its rugby team is very strong and has won an Olympic gold medal.

oceania:3.fact: A country with lots of languages: more than 800 are spoken.
oceania:3.about:
A country on the eastern half of the island of New Guinea and other islands. With more than 800 languages, it is said to be the country with the most languages in the world.
Rare birds of paradise live there, and one is shown on the flag.

#landmarks: Around the world there are amazing buildings that were made hundreds or thousands of years ago.

landmarks:0.fact: Paris, France. It was built for the World's Fair in 1889.
landmarks:0.about:
When it was built, some people were against it, saying it would spoil the view of Paris, but now it is the symbol of the city.
It is made of iron, so in summer it stretches in the heat and gets about 15 cm taller. It is repainted every 7 years.

landmarks:1.fact: New York, USA. It was a gift from France.
landmarks:1.about:
France gave it to the USA to celebrate 100 years of American independence. With its base, it is about 93 m tall.
It was first the brown colour of copper, but it changed to its green colour as it rusted.

landmarks:2.fact: China. A very long wall that took hundreds of years to build.
landmarks:2.about:
To keep out enemies from the north, it was rebuilt many times over more than 2,000 years.
The story that you can see it from space isn't true. It is too narrow to see with your eyes from space.

landmarks:3.fact: Egypt. Tombs for kings built about 4,500 years ago.
landmarks:3.about:
The biggest, the Pyramid of Khufu, is about 139 m tall (it was 147 m at first). 2.3 million stones were used to build it.
For more than 3,800 years, it was the tallest building in the world.

landmarks:4.fact: India. A very beautiful building made of white marble.
landmarks:4.about:
A tomb that an Indian emperor built for his wife after she died. It took about 20 years to finish.
People say the white marble looks pink in the morning, white at noon and golden in the moonlight at night.

landmarks:5.fact: Peru. Ruins on a mountain top 2,400 m high.
landmarks:5.about:
A town the Inca people built on a mountain top around the 15th century. The stones fit together so tightly that you can't even slip a razor blade between them.
The Spanish never found it, so it was never destroyed.

landmarks:6.fact: Rome, Italy. A huge arena built about 2,000 years ago.
landmarks:6.about:
An arena of ancient Rome that held about 50,000 people. It was built more than 1,900 years ago.
Like today's football stadiums, its entrances had numbers, so lots of people could get in and out quickly.

landmarks:7.fact: Easter Island, Chile. About 900 stone statues stand there.
landmarks:7.about:
Scientists think the people of Easter Island made them to honour their ancestors.
Most of the moai stand facing inland, not out to sea.

landmarks:8.fact: Hyōgo. A World Heritage site also called "White Heron Castle" because it is white.
landmarks:8.about:
A castle that still looks as it did more than 400 years ago. In 1993, together with Hōryū-ji, it became Japan's first World Cultural Heritage site.
Its walls are covered with white plaster, which also helps protect it from fire.

#geo-records: The highest mountain, the longest river… let's look at the Earth's world records.

geo-records:0.fact: The highest mountain in the world, 8,849 m tall. It is on the border of Nepal and China.
geo-records:0.about:
In Nepal it is called "Sagarmatha," and in Tibet "Chomolungma."
In 1953, Hillary and Tenzing were the first to stand on top. In 1975, Tabei Junko became the first woman in the world to reach the top.

geo-records:1.fact: One of the longest rivers in the world, about 6,650 km long.
geo-records:1.about: A river that flows through 11 countries in Africa. In ancient Egypt, its floods every year brought rich soil to the fields.

geo-records:2.fact: The river that carries the most water in the world.
geo-records:2.about:
About one fifth of all the river water that flows into the world's seas comes from the Amazon. Its mouth is more than 300 km wide.
Pink dolphins (Amazon river dolphins) live there too.

geo-records:3.fact: The biggest hot desert in the world, about as big as the USA.
geo-records:3.about:
People picture it as a desert of sand, but actually there is more rock and stone desert.
Thousands of years ago it was green, and pictures of giraffes and cows are still on rocks in the desert.

geo-records:4.fact: The biggest ocean. It is bigger than all the land in the world put together.
geo-records:4.about:
A huge ocean that covers about a third of the Earth's surface. It lies to the east of Japan.
Its name means "peaceful sea." It was named by Magellan.

geo-records:5.fact: The deepest lake in the world, in Russia. It is more than 1,600 m deep.
geo-records:5.about:
About 20% of the world's lake water is in this lake. It formed more than 25 million years ago, so it is also the oldest lake in the world.
The Baikal seal lives only in this lake.

geo-records:6.fact: The biggest island in the world. Most of it is covered in ice.
geo-records:6.about:
Its name means "green land," but more than 80% of it is covered in thick ice. It is part of Denmark.
People say that if all its ice melted, the world's sea level would rise by 7 m.

geo-records:7.fact: The highest waterfall in the world, in Venezuela. It is about 979 m tall.
geo-records:7.about:
A waterfall in Venezuela, South America. It falls from so high that the water turns to mist on the way down.
It is about 19 times taller than Niagara Falls.

#writing: There are many kinds of writing in the world. Some are even written from right to left!

writing:0.fact: Japanese letters that were made more than 1,000 years ago by simplifying kanji.
writing:0.about:
Hiragana were made in the Heian period by writing kanji in a quick, simple way. "あ" comes from "安," and "い" comes from "以."
Long ago they were mostly used by women, so they were also called "onnade" (women's hand).

writing:1.fact: English is written with the 26 letters of the alphabet. There are capital letters and small letters.
writing:1.about:
The word "alphabet" comes from the first two Greek letters, "alpha" and "beta."
It started as Phoenician writing more than 3,000 years ago and changed into today's shapes through Greece and Rome.

writing:2.fact: Characters that started in China more than 3,000 years ago and also came to Japan.
writing:2.about:
Many kanji come from "pictograms," pictures of things. "山" (mountain), "川" (river), "木" (tree) and "日" (sun) are some examples.
There are also kanji made in Japan, like "峠" (mountain pass), "畑" (field) and "働" (work).

writing:3.fact: The Korean alphabet. You write it by putting together parts for vowels and consonants.
writing:3.about:
In 1443, King Sejong of the Joseon dynasty made it so that anyone could easily read and write.
The shapes of the letters are based on the shape of the mouth and tongue when you make each sound.

writing:4.fact: Writing that goes from right to left. It is used for Arabic and other languages.
writing:4.about:
Writing used in more than 20 countries. The letters join up and flow along as you write.
The numbers we use (0 to 9) are called "Arabic numerals." They travelled from India through Arabia to Europe.

writing:5.fact: Letters used in Russia and other countries. Some look like the letters of the alphabet.
writing:5.about:
It was made around the 9th century, based on Greek letters. It is used for Russian, Ukrainian, Bulgarian, Mongolian and other languages.
"Р" makes an "r" sound, and "Н" makes an "n" sound. Some letters look the same as ours but are read differently.

writing:6.fact: The writing used for Hindi and other languages in India. The letters hang from a line along the top.
writing:6.about: Writing used in India. Besides Hindi, the ancient language Sanskrit is also written with these letters.

writing:7.fact: The letters of the Thai language. They have lots of round shapes.
writing:7.about:
Writing made in the 13th century. It has 44 consonant letters and also marks that show the pitch of the voice (tone).
Words are written with no spaces between them.

#japan: Japan has 47 prefectures. From north to south, every area has its own special features.

japan:0.fact: At the "Sapporo Snow Festival" in winter, huge snow statues stand in rows.
japan:0.about:
The biggest prefecture, covering about a fifth of Japan. It produces the most potatoes, milk and corn in Japan.
The culture of the Ainu, its Indigenous people, is still passed down today.

japan:1.fact: Aomori grows the most apples in Japan.
japan:1.about:
The 6 prefectures of Aomori, Iwate, Miyagi, Akita, Yamagata and Fukushima. There is lots of snow in winter, and many people grow rice.
In summer there are the "three great festivals of Tōhoku": Aomori Nebuta, Akita Kantō and Sendai Tanabata.

japan:2.fact: It has Tokyo, the capital of Japan. It is the area of Japan with the most people.
japan:2.about:
Tokyo and the 6 prefectures of Kanagawa, Saitama, Chiba, Ibaraki, Tochigi and Gunma. About a third of Japan's people live here.
Tokyo Skytree is 634 m tall. People remember it as "mu-sa-shi" (6-3-4).

japan:3.fact: It has Mt. Fuji (3,776 m), the highest mountain in Japan. It sits across Shizuoka and Yamanashi.
japan:3.about:
An area with rows of 3,000 m mountains called the Japanese Alps. Nagoya is a big car-making city.
Nagano borders more prefectures than any other prefecture in Japan (8 of them).

japan:4.fact: Kyoto was Japan's capital for more than 1,000 years.
japan:4.about:
Osaka, Kyoto, Hyōgo, Nara, Mie, Shiga and Wakayama. Nara and Kyoto have lots of old temples and shrines.
Lake Biwa in Shiga is Japan's biggest lake. Osaka is called "the nation's kitchen" and is famous for takoyaki and okonomiyaki.

japan:5.fact: Tottori has huge sand hills called the "Tottori Sand Dunes."
japan:5.about:
The 5 prefectures of Tottori, Shimane, Okayama, Hiroshima and Yamaguchi. Izumo Taisha shrine in Shimane and Miyajima (Itsukushima Shrine) in Hiroshima are famous.
Okayama is said to be the home of the Momotarō story, and it grows peaches and muscat grapes.

japan:6.fact: Kagawa is also called "Udon Prefecture." It is the home of sanuki udon.
japan:6.about:
An island made of the 4 prefectures of Tokushima, Kagawa, Ehime and Kōchi. It is joined to Honshu by bridges like the Seto Ōhashi.
Ehime's mikan oranges, Kōchi's seared bonito and Tokushima's Awa Odori dance are famous.

japan:7.fact: An area with lots of hot springs. Nagasaki is in Kyushu too.
japan:7.about:
The 7 prefectures of Fukuoka, Saga, Nagasaki, Kumamoto, Ōita, Miyazaki and Kagoshima. It has many active volcanoes, like Mt. Aso and Sakurajima.
Ōita has the most hot spring water in Japan. Nagasaki has long been the doorway for contact with other countries.

japan:8.fact: Southern islands with coral reefs in warm seas.
japan:8.about:
A prefecture with about 160 islands. Long ago it was an independent country called the "Ryūkyū Kingdom," which traded with Japan and China.
It has its own culture, like gōya chanpurū, the sanshin and Eisā dancing. The people of Okinawa are also known for living long lives.

#nagasaki: Our Nagasaki. A special city that has been connected to other countries for a very long time.

nagasaki:0.fact: In the Edo period, this was where Japan traded with the Netherlands. It was the doorway for foreign culture.
nagasaki:0.about:
A fan-shaped artificial island made in 1636. For about 200 years in the Edo period, the Netherlands was the only European country allowed to trade with Japan.
Medicine, clocks, coffee, billiards and more came to Japan through Dejima. Today, the buildings from that time have been rebuilt.

nagasaki:1.fact: A boat race that came from China. It is a summer event in Nagasaki.
nagasaki:1.about:
About 30 people ride in a long, narrow boat and row to the beat of a gong and drum.
It is said to have started around 1655, when Chinese people held a race in the harbour. Every summer, races are held in Nagasaki Harbour.

nagasaki:2.fact: A festival every October. The "dragon dance," which came from China, is famous.
nagasaki:2.about:
The autumn festival of Suwa Shrine, with almost 400 years of history. It is held every year from October 7th to 9th.
The highlights are the shows (dance offerings), which each neighbourhood performs once every 7 years. The "Jaodori" dragon dance and "Kokkodesho" are famous. The crowd asks for an encore by shouting "Motte kōi!"

nagasaki:3.fact: A festival for Chinese New Year (Spring Festival). The city fills with lanterns.
nagasaki:3.about:
A festival to celebrate Chinese New Year, the "Spring Festival." About 15,000 lanterns decorate the city.
It started as a festival for the people of Shinchi Chinatown, but now it is one of Nagasaki's big winter events.

nagasaki:4.fact: A sweet that came from Portugal and became what it is today in Nagasaki.
nagasaki:4.about:
It comes from a cake the Portuguese brought in the 16th century. Its name is said to come from the "Kingdom of Castile" in Spain.
Nagasaki castella has zarame (big grains of sugar) on the bottom.

nagasaki:5.fact: A noodle dish made up in Nagasaki by a cook from China.
nagasaki:5.about:
Around 1899, a Chinese cook, Chin Heijun, made it as a cheap, healthy meal for students from China.
"Champon" also became a word meaning "a mix of everything."

nagasaki:6.fact: You can see a beautiful night view that was chosen as one of the "New Three Great Night Views of the World."
nagasaki:6.about:
The night view from Mt. Inasa (333 m) is one of the "New Three Great Night Views of the World," along with Hong Kong and Monaco.
Lights shine on the hillside streets around the harbour, so the view looks like a giant bowl of lights.

nagasaki:7.fact: An island where Tsushima leopard cats live. On a clear day you can see South Korea.
nagasaki:7.about:
A big island of Nagasaki between Kyushu and South Korea. It is only about 50 km from Busan in South Korea.
For a very long time, it has been an island linking Japan and the Korean Peninsula. Tsushima leopard cats and Taishū horses live there.

nagasaki:8.fact: A theme park in Sasebo that looks like a town in the Netherlands.
nagasaki:8.about:
A theme park that recreates the streets of a Dutch town. Its name means "house in the woods" in Dutch.
It is famous for tulips in spring and light displays in winter.

#japanese-food: Washoku (Japanese food) became UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2013. It is popular all over the world.

japanese-food:0.fact: In the Edo period, it became popular as fast food you could eat quickly at a food stall.
japanese-food:0.about:
Fish or other toppings on rice mixed with vinegar. In the Edo period, it spread as fast food you could eat quickly at a food stall.
Now there are sushi restaurants all over the world, and some sushi, like the California roll, was invented outside Japan.

japanese-food:1.fact: It started from a Chinese noodle dish and spread across Japan in many flavours.
japanese-food:1.about:
It started from a Chinese noodle dish, and local ramen grew up all over Japan: tonkotsu in Hakata, miso in Sapporo, and champon in Nagasaki (a cousin of ramen).
"Ramen" has become an English word too.

japanese-food:2.fact: It is said to come from a dish that arrived from Portugal.
japanese-food:2.about: Fish or vegetables coated in flour batter and deep-fried. It is said to come from a dish that arrived from Portugal, and it is connected to Nagasaki too.

japanese-food:3.fact: A lunchbox classic that Japanese people have been eating for more than 1,000 years.
japanese-food:3.about:
You put umeboshi, salmon or tuna mayo inside and wrap it in nori. It is a popular item at convenience stores too.
Something like an onigiri was found at a site more than 2,000 years old.

japanese-food:4.fact: Miso is a Japanese seasoning made from soybeans.
